rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader mid-deck cannot resolve a pronoun/demonstrative/definite noun, loses the thread. Re-run this session against the live body (curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--lecture--the-gate-is-a-claim.body.txt): chunk 0 is a bare H1, no lede. Chunk 1 line 6 opens with 'the judge', 'the gate' with no prior in-file naming -- checked the module-arc-opener carve-out live: `grep -n 'gate-is-a-claim\|diagnose-and-resend\|what-packaging-is' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` -> line 50 exercise (builds verifier), line 54 lecture (packages it), line 56 this file, unbroken sequence; `grep -n 'judge\|verifier' curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` line 65 'LLM judge. Separate Claude session reads the produced work and judges it', line 74 'Push back if the verifier covers the wrong shape (a generic test suite when you needed a judge, or the reverse)' -- student built/chose a judge-shaped verifier immediately prior. Carve-out applies: referent is the artefact the student's own module-arc just produced. Rest of sequential pass: 'The check' (line 7) resolves to 'a gate'/'the gate' (line 6); 'these' (line 8) resolves to the three countermoves named earlier in the same bullet; 'The three countermoves' (line 9) restates line 8's list in the same slide, not forward/vague; 'this loop' (line 15) is anaphoric to the compare-and-teach move in the same bullet's first clauses; 'this'/'tampering' (line 34) is cataphoric, resolved by the immediately-following colon in the same sentence; 'the model'/'the gates' (line 45) and 'your gates and workflow' (line 47) continue vocabulary named on lines 6-23 and the frontier slide's own opening bullets. Harm absent throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that reads as rigour but adds nothing beyond what the slide already holds. Two prior instances of exactly this pattern are now confirmed cut, both since the last stamp (d5aa7e3d): (1) the class-(c) aphorism kicker ('A gate is one more claim in the system. Build it, then hold it to the same bar it holds the work to.', restating the H1) -- maintainer note L131 dates the cut 2026-08-25 and cites this rule by name ('check_slides.md §16 class c'); confirmed absent this session: `grep -n 'one more claim in the system' curriculum/lectures/the-gate-is-a-claim.md` -> exit 1, zero hits. (2) two further trailing clauses trimmed the same pass -- 'A gate built from the armchair catches the failures you pictured and misses the ones you have.' (would-be class-(a) doctrine restatement, re-announcing the immediately preceding 'not imagined failures' point) and 'Passing while missing the intent is a signature, not bad luck.' (would-be class-(a)/(c), restating the sentence that follows it) -- both confirmed absent via the same grep session (`grep -n 'catches the failures you pictured\|signature, not bad luck'` -> exit 1). Fresh check of the remaining body against all three classes: (a) doctrine restatement -- each of the five laws states once, no law is re-announced after already doing its work. (b) self-referential design commentary -- no line tells the reader they are inside a pedagogy; body stays first-order about gates, judges and delegation throughout. (c) aphorism kicker -- checked every chunk's final bullet as the highest-risk position: line 9 (independence unifier) and line 47 (bitter lesson) are the two candidates that could read as closers, but both introduce content beyond their header rather than restating it. Harm absent; the current body is measurably cleaner against this rule than the version this rule was written against.
